gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: She has three daughters, all of ___ are at university.
gaps.explanation: 'All of whom' refers to people after 'of'; 'all of which' is for things and 'all of them' cannot join the clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The film, ___ was shot entirely in Iceland, won three awards.
gaps.explanation: After a comma, 'that' is impossible: use 'which'.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: This is the hotel ___ we stayed last summer.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which' and needs no preposition; 'the hotel which we stayed' would be ungrammatical.

gaps.sentence: The moment ___ she saw the results, she burst into tears.
gaps.explanation: 'When' links the moment to the action; 'where' and 'why' do not fit a time noun.

gaps.sentence: The Eiffel Tower, ___ attracts millions of visitors, was completed in 1889.
gaps.explanation: For things in non-defining clauses use 'which'; 'that' is not allowed after a comma.

gaps.sentence: We interviewed a candidate ___ references were excellent.
gaps.hint: the references belong to the candidate
gaps.explanation: 'Whose references' means 'the candidate's references', so the possessive relative 'whose' is needed.
